docs.title: About
docs.text: Skip to content The name Leiðarljós is a guiding light. Leiðar is the genitive of leið , a way or course. Ljós is light. The compound is the lamp you keep on a path. The binary is ljos . Why it is not the first line The door teaches the first success: write one claim, search it back. A stranger does not need the Icelandic before that works. The name stays on the brand, the lamp mark, and this page. What the lamp is for The seat writes only on Remember: and Prefer: . Nothing is mined from chat. A sitting opens the pack, the island, and the ticket. Finish writes what the work produced. That is the path the name points at. Pronunciation Approximate English: LAY-thar-lyohs . Icelandic ð is the voiced th in this . ljos is the same word without the path. First write: /docs/start/ . Handbook: /handbook/ .

docs.title: Compare
docs.text: Skip to content Compare What packset measured packset is the standing-knowledge store in the seat. It writes only on Remember: and Prefer:. The crate explanation holds the rows. Neighbouring systems are named by protocol. Overview First write Sit Policy Harnesses Crates Reference What we measured LongMemEval_S (doi:10.48550/arXiv.2410.10813), 470 answerable questions, session-level retrieval. The pack writes claims, not harvested chat. Reproduction: scripts/longmemeval_qa.py and docs/orgmode/results/longmemeval-s-qa.org in packset. Arm hit@1 recall@5 recall@10 packset BM25+ 0.855 0.914 0.952 packset fused panel 0.889 0.949 0.981 Answer accuracy on the same 470 uses a local 7 B reader and judge (Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct Q5_K_M, LongMemEval prompts, top five sessions). CombMNZ fusion is 0.549. Lexical alone is 0.532. Labelled sessions, the ceiling for any retriever, are 0.634. MemoryAgentBench (doi:10.48550/arXiv.2507.05257), same 7 B reader. Conflict-resolution split 0.480. Published retrieval baselines on that split range from 0.155 to 0.295 with a stronger reader. Accurate-retrieval split 0.675 of 2000, against published 0.605 (BM25) and 0.651 (HippoRAG-v2). Neighbouring published numbers Two public repositories share the name agentmemory. They report different protocols. The first is session retrieval (R@5). The second is question answering with a hosted generator and a hosted judge. packset publishes both a retrieval row and a local-reader QA row so those protocols stay distinct. System Protocol Published figure Write policy rohitg00/agentmemory LongMemEval-S retrieval, R@5, all-MiniLM-L6-v2 95.2% (their COMPARISON.md) Lifecycle hooks capture transcript text JordanMcCann/agentmemory LongMemEval QA, hosted generator and judge 96.20% on 481/500 (their README) Chat over a MemoryStore packset LongMemEval_S session retrieval; QA with a local 7 B reader recall@5 0.949 fused, 0.914 lexical; QA 0.549 against a 0.634 labelled ceiling Remember: and Prefer: only The 0.949 fused recall@5 is the neighbour of the 95.2% R@5 retrieval figure. The 96.20% QA figure uses a different generator and a different judge. InjecMEM and MINJA describe the risk of writing from a transcript. packset writes only on Remember: and Prefer:. Privacy-of-write . What the other habitats answer Retrieval is one store. The seat also cites frozen product, the tracker, this-session claims, argv law, and weighted agreement. Those questions are not retrieval scores. Question Store What did the human freeze? cards What does this seat know, standing? packset What did this unit produce? deedar What does this node stand on, and who agrees? vissue What is this session handing out? claimdag May this argv run? ljos-policyd Who is right, under trust? ljos-consensus policyd is argv law ljos policy -- argv prints the line and any pack rule that matches it. ljos rule writes that law into the pack. ljos-policyd is the TCB when it is on PATH or POLICYD_BIN : it prints allow or deny. Reloading a pack is not a check. ljos-policyd docs · Argv field note . Source: packset explanation · packset

docs.title: Harnesses
docs.text:
Skip to content Harnesses Wire ljos-mcp One server, one skill, one hook. ljos onboard installs all three; ljos and ljos-mcp must be on PATH . Overview First write Sit Policy Harnesses Crates Reference One verb per runner Describe the runners on the machine once, in ~/.config/ljos/harnesses.toml . A runner registers MCP servers through a command of its own (the first table) or through a config file it reads (the other two). A table names one of those two, the directory it loads skills from, and the settings file it reads hooks from. ljos onboard --example prints the shape. [[harness]] name = "runner-c" config = "~/.runner-c/config.toml" marker = "[mcp_servers.ljos]" snippet = "
[mcp_servers.ljos]
command = "{server}"
args = []
startup_timeout_sec = 30
env = { LJOS_SEAT = "{name}", GROK_SESSION_ID = "${GROK_SESSION_ID}" }
" [[harness]] name = "runner-a" register = ["runner-a", "mcp", "add", "-s", "user", "ljos", "-e", "LJOS_SEAT={name}", "-e", "GROK_SESSION_ID=${GROK_SESSION_ID}", "--", "{server}"] registered = ["runner-a", "mcp", "get", "ljos"] skills = "~/.runner-a/skills" hooks = "~/.runner-a/settings.json" [[harness]] name = "runner-b" config = "~/.runner-b/config.toml" marker = "[mcp_servers.ljos]" snippet = "
[mcp_servers.ljos]
command = "{server}"
args = []
env = { LJOS_SEAT = "{name}", GROK_SESSION_ID = "${GROK_SESSION_ID}" }
" skills = "~/.runner-b/skills" hooks = "~/.runner-b/hooks.json" Then, for each: $ ljos onboard --harness runner-a ok host key /home/you/.config/deedar/host.key exists ok runner-a mcp ran runner-a mcp add -s user ljos -- /home/you/.cargo/bin/ljos-mcp ok hook memory hook: add it on UserPromptSubmit in /home/you/.runner-a/settings.json ok skill wrote /home/you/.runner-a/skills/ljos/SKILL.md $ ljos doctor | grep runner Three things land. The server, so the runner has the seat's tools. The skill is the protocol ljos protocol prints: which store answers which question, the order of verbs in a sitting, the refusals worth knowing. The memory hook runs before each prompt . The runner pipes the prompt to ljos hook . The memories it activates come back as context, preferences first, each once per session. Do not add PreToolUse to search the pack. A turn issues many tool calls and one prompt. On a tool call, ljos hook only decides rules (deny a force-push). Searching on every tool is what made Grok wait 20s and print Ljos Ljos Due . --dry-run reports and writes nothing. {server} in a table is the path to ljos-mcp , {name} the runner's name. Passing LJOS_SEAT={name} to the server, as the tables above do, makes each runner claim and vote under its own name. Two runners on one host share the one pack and the one tracker. ljos sitting without --assignee takes that name. Neither is refused as busy for what the other holds. A persona named with as speaks over both. Any other runner $ ljos onboard --harness json { "mcpServers": { "ljos": { "type": "stdio", "command": "/home/you/.cargo/bin/ljos-mcp", "args": [], "env": { "LJOS_SEAT": "runner", "GROK_SESSION_ID": "${GROK_SESSION_ID}" } } } } $ ljos protocol > instructions.md Paste the entry where the runner keeps its MCP servers. Cursor, Pi, and the rest take this shape. Put the protocol where the agent reads its instructions. If the runner has hooks, a command hook on prompts that runs ljos hook completes the set. Grok: copy scripts/grok/ljos.json to ~/.grok/hooks/ once. The JSON only names ljos hook . The prompt's pack is held and emitted on PostToolUse , which Grok delivers. Later cargo binstall ljos is the new hook. Name ljos-mcp on PATH; bump LJOS_MCP_GENERATION in config.toml to respawn. Crate page: Grok Build . The two verbs an agent runs ljos sitting <issue> --assignee <name> # doctor, cards, due, island, recall, timeline, claim ljos finish <issue> --lesson "..." [--outcome <option>] # remember, fire, complete, learn One verb opens a sitting in the protocol's order and stops at the first store that does not answer. One closes it. The loop that makes the seat a memory runs every time. It does not wait for someone to remember the steps. Cite a deed on a ticket ljos evidence deed-… ljos deed <id> --add deed-… ljos recall <id> Citation is not a merge. Completing a session node does not close the ticket.

docs.title: The island
docs.text: Skip to content Island The cluster this task touches. A persona is a view over everything. An island is the linked claims this piece of work involves. Overview Install Island Open a ticket Crates Fig. 1 landfold of the live seat pack: 148 atoms (74 lesson, 12 preference, 60 persona, 2 trust). 384-D bge-small, landfold embed --dot --fun-hd asinh,0.56 --center , stress 0.021. Cream is the pack. Gold is the docs activation island; rings are seeds. Fig. 2 the same 148 atoms, folded from the link graph: pairwise distance is 1 − weight on an edge and 2 off-edge. landfold embed --similarity --fun-hd asinh,0.5 --center , stress 0.075. Hop-PHATE stacked 148 points onto 44 positions; this fold keeps 148 unique. Gold is the docs activation island. How it is built The pack links each claim to the claims it shares names with. Those links form clusters. ljos island TASK takes the top search hits as seeds and spreads activation two hops: half lost per hop, divided by fan-out. The cluster comes back strongest first. That is spreading activation over a semantic network (Collins and Loftus, doi:10.1037/0033-295X.82.6.407). Fig. 1 folds sentence vectors (bge-small, cosine as --dot , Ceriotti asinh at the median pairwise scale). Fig. 2 folds the weighted link graph. Gold is the docs activation cluster, not a 3-gram hash. How use shapes it When the seat uses an island, ljos island --fire moves each fired pair's weight toward one and fades the rest (Hebb with Oja's term). The next cue like this one walks a heavier path. The weights travel in a handover. Search ranking is separate On LongMemEval the island lost as a ranker (hit@1 0.377 against the fused panel's 0.889). Activation flows to hubs. The island is orientation and what fires together after use. The verb lives on the pack. The seat prints the strongest eight when it opens a ticket. The fold is landfold . Field note: ljos explanation .

docs.title: Argv law
docs.text: Skip to content Policy May this command line run? Ask with uv . A Janet pack can deny more after the binary. It cannot allow what the binary denied. Overview First write Sit Policy Harnesses Crates Reference uv $ uvx ljos-policyd check -- uv run pytest allow $ uvx ljos-policyd check -- sudo id deny sudo First matching deny wins. Exit 2. exec runs the line only on allow. Janet (defn check [argv] (when (has-prefix? (get argv 0) "sudo") (deny "sudo"))) A Janet pack denies more after this binary. It cannot allow what the binary denied. The seat composes it: ljos policy -- uv run pytest . The hook ljos hook reads the action about to happen. The binary is the gate. The pack rule is memory beside it. Crate site: ljos-policyd . Field note: reloading a pack is not a check .

docs.title: Privacy-of-write
docs.text: Skip to content Privacy-of-write Extract-on-write is refused A seat that harvests a transcript is a different product. leiðarljós writes only on Remember: and Prefer:. Overview First write Sit Policy Harnesses Crates Reference Only explicit claims Remember: and Prefer: are the pack writes. The text is the claim. It is not parsed out of a sitting. Empty text is refused. Cards stay frozen USER.md and MEMORY.md are a human freeze. ljos cards prints them. It never writes them. Overflow is an error, not a prompt to dump more. The harness memory file is dead Do not write a client memory file and call it standing knowledge. The pack is the pack. The cards are the cards. Citation is not a merge An accession can be named in more than one habitat. That does not pour the habitats into one store. Opening the bytes is a deed question. Completing is not closing ljos complete finishes a session node. The cited ticket stays open until the tracker says otherwise.

docs.text: Skip to content Reference CLI and MCP ljos is the seat. Habitats keep their own CLIs. Completing a session node does not close a ticket. Overview First write Sit Policy Harnesses Crates Reference CLI Verb Habitat Does ljos sitting ID seat Open: doctor, cards, due, island, recall, timeline, claim. ljos finish ID seat Close: remember, fire, complete, learn. Does not close the ticket. ljos remember TEXT packset POST one explicit claim. Needs PACKSET_URL . ljos prefer TEXT packset Same write path, kind preference. ljos search QUERY packset Retrieve standing knowledge. ljos evidence ACCESSION deedar Frozen product bytes. ljos current ACCESSION deedar Current pointer. ljos deed ID [--add ACCESSION] tracker Cite. Not a merge. Crate: vissue. ljos recall ID tracker Working set. ljos vote ID [--for CHOICE] tracker Ballots. ljos claim NODE claimdag This-session CAS. ljos complete NODE claimdag Does not close a ticket. ljos cards cards Read USER.md / MEMORY.md . Never writes. ljos policy -- ARGV policyd Argv law. Does not reload a pack. ljos consensus ID consensus crate DeGroot / ODE, then the tracker verb. MCP ljos-mcp execs ljos . Tool names match the verbs, including ljos_vote . Tool Arguments Does ljos_remember text Standing knowledge. Never extract-on-write. ljos_prefer text Standing preference. Never extract-on-write. ljos_search query Retrieve via PACKSET_URL . ljos_evidence accession deedar evidence. ljos_current accession deedar current tip. ljos_deed issue , optional add Cite an accession on a tracker node. ljos_recall issue Working set. ljos_claim node Claim a claimdag node. ljos_complete node Complete a claimdag node. Does not close a ticket. ljos_cards — Read-only cards. ljos_policy argv Print argv. Reload is not a check. ljos_consensus id ljos-consensus then the tracker verb. Not a vote count. docs.title: Sit and finish
docs.text: Skip to content Sit Open a ticket. Print the island. An island is the cluster of linked claims this task activates. Completing the session node does not close the ticket. Overview First write Sit Policy Harnesses Crates Reference 1. Point at scratch stores A first sitting should not touch a live tracker. Export the roots, start the pack writer, and ask doctor. $ mkdir -p /tmp/seat && cd /tmp/seat && git init -q $ export VISSUE_ROOT=/tmp/seat/tracker DEEDAR_URL=file:///tmp/seat/deeds $ export CLAIMDAG_DIR=/tmp/seat/claims PACKSET_URL=http://127.0.0.1:18761 $ packsetd --port 18761 --home /tmp/seat-pack & $ ljos doctor 2. Make a ticket and sit it sitting prints seven sections and stops at the first store that does not answer: doctor, cards, due, the island the title activates, recall, timeline, then the claim. After the sitting, read each due row and run ljos graded ID (or --lapsed ). The clock does not move until you grade. Shared names you , grok , seat , and agent become the session prefix. Two conversations then do not share one slot. $ id=$(vissue create -p demo "Ship the fuse change?" -q) $ ljos sitting $id --assignee alice == doctor ... == timeline ... == claim gen=2 3. Cite what the work produced A deed is frozen bytes. The ticket cites the accession. Citation is not a merge. $ echo 'fn main() {}' > patch.rs $ deedar create file --name "the fuse patch" --path patch.rs --agent you $ ljos deed $id --add deed-file-the-fuse-patch 4. Finish The lesson is remembered. The island fires. The session node completes. An outcome, when named, rewrites trust. The tracker issue is still open until someone closes it there. $ ljos finish $id --lesson "The fuse patch shipped as one file. Nothing else moved." remembered ... completed the session node ... as done Agreement is ljos consensus over ljos-consensus on crates.io. The seat crate walks the same loop: ljos getting started . Field note: completing is not closing .

docs.title: First write
docs.text: Skip to content Start Write one claim. Search it back. A reader who has never used the seat finishes this page with one lesson in the pack. Search returns the same text. A review clock is running on it. Overview First write Sit Policy Harnesses Crates Reference 1. Install the binaries this walk uses $ cargo binstall ljos ljos-mcp packset packset-daemon deedar-cli claimdag-cli vissue-cli ljos-consensus ljos-policyd $ command -v ljos ljos-mcp packset packsetd deedar claimdag vissue ljos-consensus ljos-policyd The homepage installs ljos alone. This walk needs the rest of the seat. You should see nine paths. If packsetd is missing, step 3 has no writer. Without cargo-binstall , cargo install of the same nine names works. Other runners: Harnesses . 2. Remember without a writer fails $ ljos remember "the default fuse is CombMNZ" Error: remember: the pack writer did not answer at http://127.0.0.1:8761 ... That error is the first success. The seat will not invent a store, and it does not report a writer that is down as an empty pack. 3. Start a scratch writer $ export PACKSET_URL=http://127.0.0.1:18761 $ packsetd --port 18761 --home /tmp/seat-pack & $ ljos doctor ok pack http://127.0.0.1:18761 workspace seat Do not call packset ensure against the default port if a writer is already up. That joins the live pack. If the pack row says no, stop. 4. Write one claim, then retrieve it $ ljos remember "the default fuse is CombMNZ" $ ljos search fuse 1.0000 lesson 156eb2be9898... the default fuse is CombMNZ $ ljos due 0 due; 1 scheduled, next at ... You should see kind lesson and the same sentence in the search hit. A review is scheduled a day out. Tomorrow ljos due lists the claim. ljos graded ID (or --lapsed ) moves the clock. 5. Prefer is the same path $ ljos prefer "never extract on write" $ ljos search extract 1.0000 preference ... never extract on write Next: sit and finish . The crate tutorial runs memory, agreement, and a handover: ljos getting started .

docs.title: The pin is an accession.
docs.text: The pin is an accession. Back to the field DEEDAR_URL names the directory ( file:// plus a path). Unset, the command has nowhere to write. deedar create file needs --id , --path , and --agent . The pin is deed-… or sha256: . ljos evidence asks deedar for the bytes. ljos deed ID --add ACCESSION names the accession on a ticket. It does not paste the product into the ticket. The pack may name the same accession. That is not a merge. If the store is empty, that is an error. Frozen product / deedar

docs.title: A vote count is not consensus.
docs.text: A vote count is not consensus. Back to the field ljos vote ID --for OPTION records a ballot. One ballot per identity; --as NAME casts as a persona. A recast replaces. A missing identity is no. ljos consensus ID is the seat verb: the model crate, then the tracker, both under the trust rows the pack holds that apply to the issue's topic and every persona's anchor. The model is DeGroot / Friedkin–Johnsen, or bounded confidence when the issue is tagged broad , or the Seldon ODE when --seldon and seldon are on PATH. Every outcome says how the group split, in polarization and disagreement; a count says only who won. On a hard question add a forecast beside the ballot, ljos predict ID --expect OPTION ; with two or more forecasts the settle also names the surprisingly popular answer, the option whose actual share most exceeds its forecast, and shows each voter's standing from the rows. The rows are memory. ljos learn ID --outcome OPTION shrinks the voters the outcome refuted and loosens the anchors of refuted personas; ljos calibrate -p PROJECT writes rows from the project's history when nobody names an outcome; ljos trust FROM TO W --about DOMAIN sets one by hand, scoped. Under equal rows a settle is a count. A panel is one subagent per persona, each started from ljos brief NAME ID , each casting one ballot as itself, then the settle. ljos persona NAME --anchor A --view TEXT --about DOMAIN writes the persona once; it stays in the pack. Four green ticks are a host rule for landing work. They are not the model. Do not report a count as if it were the crate. consensus · ljos · seldon-code

docs.title: Reloading a pack is not a check.
docs.text: Reloading a pack is not a check. Back to the field $ uvx ljos-policyd check -- uv run pytest allow A Janet pack can deny more after that verdict: (defn check [argv] (when (has-prefix? (get argv 0) "sudo") (deny "sudo"))) ljos-policyd check -- argv is the TCB when the binary is on PATH (or POLICYD_BIN ). It prints allow or deny . The harness hook and ljos policy call it. The Janet pack cannot allow what the binary denied. ljos policy -- argv prints the line, then the TCB verdict if the binary answered, then any pack rule that matches, then what the pack knows that bears on it. It does not reload a Janet pack. Absence of the binary is not a deny. Doctor names the row. ljos hook is the same answer for a policy layer or a runner: pipe the action about to happen (the runner's hook JSON, or the plain argv) and the memories it activates come back, standing preferences first, as the runner's additionalContext or as plain lines. Nothing to say is no output; the hook never blocks an action. ljos onboard installs it on a runner's tool-call and prompt events. Memory reaches the agent at the point of action, without being asked for. When the session ends, the memories the hook injected during it fire together, so what served one sitting is wired for the next. Law can live in the pack: ljos rule 'PATTERN' --verdict deny|ask --why "..." writes a glob over the command line with a verdict, and the hook returns it as the runner's permission decision while ljos policy prints it beside the line. A rule is memory: dated, supersedable, exported in handovers. Edit a pack rule only when argv law itself changes. Do not write comments, dates, ticket ids, or sitting notes into it. If the binary is down, leave the pack rules alone. Other projects may speak one habitat and ignore ljos . Habitats · Compare

docs.title: Overflow is an error.
docs.text: Overflow is an error. Back to the field ljos cards prints USER.md and MEMORY.md from --dir (default . ). A missing file prints nothing. The command never creates those files and never writes them. Cards answer one question: what did the human freeze? Overflow is an error, not a prompt to dump more. A client scrapbook is not a card. Read the cards at the start of a sitting. If they are empty, leave them empty. Habitats

docs.title: Completing is not closing.
docs.text: Completing is not closing. Back to the field ljos sitting ISSUE --assignee NAME opens the sitting: doctor, cards, due, island, recall, timeline, claim, in that order, stopping at the first store that does not answer. The assignee is a name; it maps to one actor. One live claim per name. A second claim is refused with the issue the name still holds and the two verbs that free it: ljos complete finishes it, ljos release hands it back unfinished. ljos finish ISSUE --lesson "..." [--outcome OPTION] closes the sitting: remember, fire the island, complete, learn. A later sitting on the same issue reopens its node and takes it; the ledger keeps the earlier completion. Completing a node does not close a ticket. The tracker is the graph. Create and claim tickets through vissue . Never hand-edit issues.org . Crate docs: vissue.rgoswami.me . File before you speak. An audit with no ids is unfinished work. A leftover that does not fit this sitting is a child ticket, then the original work continues. Session work / claimdag

docs.title: Remember is a speech act.
docs.text: Remember is a speech act. Back to the field ljos remember POSTs one lesson to /v1/atoms . ljos prefer POSTs one preference. The writer is found on 127.0.0.1:8761 with nothing set; packset ensure starts one. A writer that is down is an error, never an empty pack. The seat's memory is one workspace, seat , from any directory. The pack's own command line keys a workspace to the git remote of the directory it stands in; the seat does not, because a seat is one memory across every repository it works in. PACKSET_WORKSPACE names another on purpose. Search is GET /v1/search on the seat's workspace. It does not open a deed. A transcript is not a source. If you did not say Remember: or Prefer: , the pack did not change. Every recalled memory carries its age ( [lesson, 3 weeks ago] ), and the hook's lessons run oldest to newest behind the preferences; read them as a timeline, a later one revises an earlier one. ljos timeline ISSUE is the tracker's logbook, the cited deeds and the activated memories as one dated list, oldest first, with the gap between lines. ljos search TOPIC --as-of TIME is the pack as it stood then. A lesson that rewrites an earlier one (same opening words, a new object) closes the earlier one's window on arrival, and remember says so. ljos consolidate runs the same rule over what is already held and reports the pairs; --apply closes them. Run it after ljos receive --import . ljos island CUE is what a task touches; ljos hubs is what the pack turns on by its own links, a weighted PageRank over them: the natural list to pin, to review first, or to carry when the whole pack is too much. Every claim enters the review clock on write. ljos due lists what is due and ends with one line on the clock; ljos graded ID moves it. A claim never graded sinks in search as its retrievability falls. If packset status says up and remember hangs or returns 400, the writer is wedged. packset stop , then packset ensure . Do not dump the sitting into a card. Privacy-of-write

docs.title: Write one claim. Search it back.
docs.text: Skip to content First write Write one claim. Search it back. Write one claim How sitting works Fig. 1 A sitting. Seven sections. Completing does not close the ticket. specimen sitting remember policy $ ljos sitting demo-k29f --assignee alice == doctor == cards == due == island == recall == timeline == claim gen=2 install Copy cargo binstall ljos ljos-mcp packset packset-daemon deedar-cli claimdag-cli vissue-cli ljos-consensus ljos-policyd ljos alone cannot remember. Start a scratch writer with packsetd --port 18761 --home /tmp/seat-pack . The walk: First write . The name: leiðarljós . The loop Write. Sit. Finish. 01 Remember One claim, two sentences at most, stored as written. ljos remember and ljos prefer are the only pack writes. Nothing is mined from a transcript. 02 Sit ljos sitting opens: doctor, cards, due, island, recall, timeline, claim. Cite what the work produced. Completing here does not close the ticket. 03 Finish ljos finish remembers the lesson, fires the island, completes the session node, and learns from an outcome when one is named.
